gloss: to tackle; to grapple with; to work on

definitions.explanation: To engage seriously with a problem, task, or project.
Originally from sumo, meaning to engage in a match. Now mostly used figuratively.

examples.japanese: {環境|かんきょう}{問題|もんだい}に{真剣|しんけん}に{取|と}り{組|く}む{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to seriously tackle environmental issues.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいプロジェクトに{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: I'm working on a new project.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}に{積極的|せっきょくてき}に{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: The company is actively working on work-style reform.

notes:
{取|と}り{組|く}む is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}) formed from {取|と}る (to take) + {組|く}む (to grapple). Originally a sumo term, it now mainly means to engage seriously with tasks or problems.

ASPECT (ている):
{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる indicates ongoing engagement with a task or problem. This is the most common form.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [problem/task]に{取|と}り{組|く}む — to tackle/work on [problem/task]
- [problem]に{真剣|しんけん}に{取|と}り{組|く}む — to seriously tackle [problem]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {課題|かだい}に{取|と}り{組|く}む (work on a task/challenge)
- {問題|もんだい}に{取|と}り{組|く}む (tackle a problem)
- {研究|けんきゅう}に{取|と}り{組|く}む (engage in research)
- {改革|かいかく}に{取|と}り{組|く}む (work on reform)

NOTE: Takes the particle に, not を, because it's intransitive.
